t.4.48.1: Then the greatly wise Aṅgada, weary himself, consoled all the vānaras and slowly spoke these words to them.
t.4.48.2: Forests, mountains and rivers, impassable places and dense thickets, ravines and mountain caves have all been searched by us on every side.
t.4.48.3: Here and there, searching together with us, Jānakī is not to be seen, nor is that rākṣasa by whom Sītā, who resembles a daughter of the gods, was carried off.
t.4.48.4: Much of our time has already passed, and Sugrīva is stern in his commands. Therefore, let you all, keeping together, search on every side.
t.4.48.6: Freedom from despondency, skill, and an unconquered mind, these, they say, bring about the accomplishment of a task; therefore I say this to you.
t.4.48.5: Casting off weariness and grief, and the drowsiness that has come over you, search in such a way that we may find Sītā, the daughter of Janaka.
t.4.48.7: Even now let the forest-dwellers search this impassable forest. Casting off weariness, let this entire forest be searched once again.
t.4.48.8: The fruit of an action that is being carried out is surely seen. Enough of giving way to despondency, for gloom is not fitting for us.
t.4.48.9: O monkeys, King Sugrīva is wrathful and stern in his punishment; he is ever to be feared, and so is the great-souled Rāma.
t.4.48.10: This has been said to you for your own good, O monkeys; let it be done if it pleases you. Or else let it be said what is fitting for all of us.
t.4.48.11: Having heard Aṅgada's words, Gandhamādana spoke in a voice indistinct, worn down by thirst and fatigue.
t.4.48.12: The words that Aṅgada has spoken are indeed fitting for you all; they are both beneficial and agreeable, so let what he has said be done.
t.4.48.13: Once more let us search the mountains, the caves and the clefts as well, the deserted forests and the mountain springs.
t.4.48.14: Let all of you search the forest and the mountain fastnesses everywhere, all of them, just as they were indicated by the great-souled Sugrīva.
t.4.48.15: Then, rising up once more, those mighty vānaras roamed the southern quarter, thick with the forests of the Vindhya.
t.4.48.16: And those monkeys, having climbed the splendid silver mountain, which resembled an autumn cloud and was full of peaks and caves...
t.4.48.17: There the best of the monkeys, longing to catch sight of Sītā, searched through the lovely grove of lodhra trees and the groves of saptaparṇa trees.
t.4.48.18: Having climbed to its summit, those monkeys of great valour, weary as they were, did not see Vaidehī, the beloved queen of Rāma.
t.4.48.19: Having surveyed that mountain with its many caves, the monkeys climbed down, looking about on every side.
t.4.48.20: Then, having descended to the ground, weary and dispirited, they stood there for a moment and then took shelter at the foot of a tree.
t.4.48.21: Having rested for a moment, their weariness somewhat relieved, they set out once again to search the entire southern quarter.
t.4.48.22: Those bulls among the monkeys, led by Hanumān, having set out, first of all roamed the Vindhya itself on every side.
